findings.title: Captured metadata can forge deterministic sensor provenance
findings.description: The factory treats every finding nested under `deterministicEvidence` as deterministic and copies the supplied sensor and producer identifiers into the canonical report. It does not verify that the evidence originated from the configured sensor registry or a separate trusted record. Consequently, any party able to influence `ReviewMetaJson` can make arbitrary findings appear machine-produced, undermining the report's provenance and integrity.
findings.recommendation: Obtain deterministic evidence from a separately trusted data structure keyed to the configured sensor registry, or authenticate and validate the captured evidence before projection. Reject unknown sensor identities and do not infer trusted provenance solely from JSON nesting.

findings.title: Malformed metadata can abort canonical report generation
findings.description: Only root parsing is guarded. Subsequent `AsArray`, `AsObject`, and `GetValue<string>` calls assume exact JSON types and can throw when fields have unexpected shapes. A single malformed captured snapshot can therefore prevent construction of the entire terminal report rather than being rejected or represented as an invalid observation.
findings.recommendation: Validate the complete metadata schema before projection, or replace throwing conversions with type checks and `TryGetValue` logic. Handle invalid individual observations deterministically without terminating generation of the whole report.
